question: Which Linux companion app track and ownership/release/security path should OpenClaw accept before treating #75 as resolved?
rationale: Current main already covers Windows Hub, but Linux remains unimplemented and the open Linux PRs make different language, packaging, dependency, and security tradeoffs that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Choose a Linux app track
options.body: Keep #75 open while app/platform owners select one Linux implementation path and require security, packaging, and real desktop proof before merge.

options.title: Split into narrower milestones
options.body: Keep this umbrella open but create scoped Linux follow-ups for tray/status, gateway setup, notifications, packaging, and node capabilities before accepting a large app PR.

options.title: Defer Linux companion apps
options.body: Close or freeze the Linux app work for now and direct contributors to external/community apps until core security and setup priorities settle.

recommendation.title: Choose a Linux app track
recommendation.body: Keep #75 open while app/platform owners select one Linux implementation path and require security, packaging, and real desktop proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue was opened by steipete, and the discussion shows steipete setting the GTK-native Linux direction and Windows Hub follow-up expectations.
